plan: [I will bid a fraction of my value in stage 1. This fraction will be 0.75. This is because I want to win if the other bidders bid low, but I don't want to overpay if they bid high. Bidding slightly below my value allows me to secure a win at a profitable price if the other bidders have lower values, while also minimizing my risk of overpaying substantially if another bidder has a higher value. This approach balances the desire to win with the need to protect my profit margin.]

[My value is $21, which is outside the typical range of $0-$20. Given this unusually high value, I should aim to win the auction. I will bid aggressively in Stage 1 to ensure I stay in the auction until the price is high enough that the other bidders, with likely lower values, drop out. Since the values are capped at $20 for others, I will bid $20. This guarantees I win unless someone else also has a value above $20, which is unlikely. ]

[My value is $8. I want to maximize my profit. In the ascending clock auction, I want to stay in as long as the price is less than my value. If I bid my value, and another bidder bids higher, I will lose, which is fine. If I bid lower than my value, I might win at a lower price, but I might also exit too early and miss out on potential profit. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $8. This will ensure I stay in the auction as long as the price is below my value, maximizing potential profit.]
